mainTopic: The ban on raising small animals (בהמה דקה): its limits, stories of its seriousness, related leniencies, and its adoption in Babylonia
overview: This amud is about the rabbinic ban on raising small animals like sheep and goats in ארץ ישראל, because they graze in other people's fields. A ברייתא allows a butcher to hold animals before slaughter for up to thirty days. It also reports that רבן גמליאל allowed 'raising' them. The גמרא corrects this wording: he only allowed keeping one briefly, tied to the bed legs so it cannot graze. A story follows about a sick חסיד who kept a goat for its milk. His friends treated the goat as a sin, and he admitted it was his only sin. רבי ישמעאל tells how his family lost its wealth by leading animals through another person's field and by judging money cases with one judge. Another ברייתא lets a repentant shepherd sell his flock gradually and limits sweeping vows to what is fitting. It also extends the ban to small wild animals, though רבי ישמעאל allows pest-catching animals like cats and חולדות סנאים. Finally, רב says Babylonia took on the same ban. רב אדא בר אהבה curses רב הונא for keeping guarded animals, and a new story begins about רב, שמואל and רב אסי at a celebration, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A butcher may hold animals before slaughter, up to thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a butcher may buy small animals and keep them before slaughtering, as long as the last one is not kept for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: A butcher may buy animals and slaughter them, and buy more and keep them for a while, as long as he does not keep the last one of them for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is still going. It adds a special allowance for a butcher, who needs a supply of animals ready to slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on raising small animals long-term, because they damage other people's fields. A butcher's short holding period is not 'raising'. The thirty-day limit marks where 'waiting to be slaughtered' would start to become 'raising'.

keyTerms.meaning: Buys and holds the animal for a while
The last one, the animal still waiting its turn

phrases.english: And the butcher may buy and slaughter,
buy and keep them for a while,
provided that he does not keep
the last one among them for thirty days.
phrases.notes: עגונה literally means 'held back'. It's the last animal of the group, still waiting to be slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about raising small animals in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher may buy and hold small animals before slaughter, but must not keep the last one for thirty days.

steps.title: The students ask רבן גמליאל about raising animals, and he permits it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reports that רבן גמליאל's students asked whether one may raise small animals, and he answered that it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבן גמליאל: what is the law about raising small animals? He told them: it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a question and answer between רבן גמליאל and his students. This sets up the next move, because his answer sounds surprising.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As the words read, רבן גמליאל seems to allow full-scale raising of small animals. That is exactly what our משנה forbids, so a problem is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: To raise animals, as a herd kept long-term

phrases.english: His students asked Rabban Gamliel:
What is the law about raising small animals?
He said to them: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As first quoted, רבן גמליאל permits raising small animals.

steps.title: But our משנה forbids raising them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא interrupts: how can רבן גמליאל permit raising small animals when our משנה says one may not raise them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: one may not raise small animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the ברייתא to raise a challenge. רבן גמליאל's answer seems to contradict our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה plainly says 'אין מגדלין': one may not raise small animals in ארץ ישראל. A ruling that 'raising is permitted' clashes head-on with it, so the wording of the ברייתא must be wrong somehow.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: One may not raise them!
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which forbids raising small animals in ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's ruling that raising small animals is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה explicitly forbids raising small animals, so a ruling that permits it contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: They really asked about keeping an animal briefly, tied to the bed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the students asked about keeping an animal for a while, not raising it. רבן גמליאל allowed this if the animal stays tied to the bed legs and does not graze with the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they asked him: what is the law about keeping an animal for a while? He told them: it is permitted, as long as it does not go out and graze with the flock. Instead, one ties it to the legs of the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by correcting what the students actually asked. Then it goes back to quoting רבן גמליאל's answer, with its conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long-term raising stays forbidden, just as the משנה says. Briefly keeping one animal is allowed, because the worry is damage to others' fields. Tying it to the bed removes that worry, since it never goes out to graze.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what they asked him; it signals a correction
To keep for a while, short-term

steps.whatToRemember: Raising small animals in ארץ ישראל is forbidden, but keeping one briefly is allowed if it is tied up at home and cannot graze in others' fields.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up לגדל and לשהות. לגדל means raising animals long-term, which is forbidden. לשהות means holding one for a short time, which is allowed with conditions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the reason behind the ban: the damage grazing animals cause. Once that damage is prevented, keeping the animal is allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they asked him:
What is the law about keeping one for a while?
He said to them: It is permitted,
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא goes back to quoting רבן גמליאל's answer from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: provided that it does not go out
and graze among the flock;
rather, one ties it to the legs of the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3 by correcting the wording of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the ברייתא (לגדל becomes לשהות)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל permitted raising small animals, against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only permitted keeping an animal briefly, tied to the bed so it cannot graze, which fits the משנה.

steps.title: The story of the sick חסיד and the goat tied to his bed
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא tells of a חסיד with heart pain. The doctors said only fresh warm milk every morning would help, so a goat was tied to his bed and he drank from it each morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: there was a story about a certain חסיד who was groaning from pain in his heart. They asked the doctors, who said: there is no cure for him except to drink warm milk every morning. So they brought him a goat, tied it to the legs of his bed, and he drank from it every morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a story. This sets up what comes next, since the story is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat is tied to the bed legs, exactly the method רבן גמליאל just allowed for keeping an animal briefly. Even so, this is a pious man keeping a small animal at home, so the reader should expect the story to continue on this very issue.

keyTerms.meaning: Warm milk, fresh from the animal

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with a certain pious man
who was groaning from his heart,
and they asked the doctors, and they said:
There is no remedy for him
unless he suckles warm milk
every morning.
And they brought him a goat
and tied it for him to the legs of the bed,
and he would suckle from it
every morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story using the same 'tied to the bed legs' method allowed in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick חסיד kept a goat tied to his bed for medicinal milk, and the story continues beyond this point.

steps.title: The friends call the goat an armed bandit
steps.stepSummary: The חסיד's friends come to visit him, see the goat tied to his bed, and turn back, calling it an armed bandit in his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some days later his friends came to visit him. When they saw the goat tied to the legs of the bed, they turned around and said: 'There is an armed bandit in this man's house, and we are going in to see him?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story of the sick חסיד. His friends see the goat and refuse to go in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the goat was tied up and was not grazing, the friends still treated it as something stolen and dangerous. A small animal like a goat normally eats from other people's fields, so they saw keeping it as being like housing a robber.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'armed bandit' is the goat, not a person. The friends are describing the goat that way.

phrases.english: Days later, his friends came in to visit him.
When they saw that goat
tied to the legs of the bed,
they turned back and said:
There is an armed bandit in this man's house,
phrases.notes: They mean the goat. Goats tend to eat from other people's fields, so it's like a robber.

phrases.english: and we are going in to him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 5 about the חסיד who kept a goat for its milk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping a small animal is so serious that the חסיד's friends compared it to housing an armed bandit, even when it is kept for medical reasons.

steps.title: The goat was his only sin
steps.stepSummary: The friends investigate and find no sin in him except the goat, and before he dies the חסיד himself admits this.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat and examined his deeds and found no sin in him except the sin of that goat. He himself said when he was dying: 'I know that I have no sin except the sin of that goat, because I went against the words of my colleagues.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Both the friends and the חסיד himself agree that the goat was his one sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a fully righteous man with a real medical need is counted as having sinned by keeping the goat. This shows how firmly the חכמים held to the rule against raising small animals in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of his death
I went against the words of

steps.whatToRemember: The story teaches that keeping a small animal against the חכמים' rule counts as a real sin, even for a חסיד who did it to heal himself.

phrases.english: They sat and investigated,
and they found nothing in him except
that sin of that goat.
And he himself also said at the time of his death:
I know that there is no sin in me
except the sin of that goat,
for I went against the words of my colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story by confirming that the friends were right: the goat was a sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keeping the goat went against the חכמים and counted as a sin.

steps.title: Why רבי ישמעאל's family estates were destroyed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says his wealthy family lost everything because they grazed animals in a way that harmed others and judged money cases with a single judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: My father's family were wealthy landowners in the Upper גליל. Why were they destroyed? Because they grazed animals in the forests and judged money cases with one judge. Even though their forests were near their houses, there was a small field in between, and they led the animals on a path through it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching. רבי ישמעאל gives a real example of a family punished for how they grazed their animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grazing itself was in their own forests, so it seems allowed. The problem was the small private field in between, which the animals walked through and damaged. Their second fault was judging money cases with only one judge, even though such cases normally need a court of three.
steps.confusionAlert: Their sin was not grazing in their own forests. It was walking the animals through someone else's small field on the way there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
Among the wealthy property owners in the Upper Galilee
was my father's family.
And why were they destroyed?
Because they grazed animals in the forests,
and they judged money cases with a single judge.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ לָהֶם חוֹרָשִׁים סָמוּךְ לְבָתֵּיהֶם,
phrases.english: And even though they had forests near their houses,
there was a small field,
and they would lead the animals on a path through it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second example of the harm that comes from letting animals graze where they damage other people's land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Letting animals cross another person's field, even on the way to your own land, is serious enough to bring ruin. So is judging money cases with one judge.

steps.title: A repentant shepherd may sell his flock gradually
steps.stepSummary: A shepherd who does תשובה, and a גר who inherits dogs and pigs, are not forced to sell everything at once. They may sell little by little.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: A shepherd who repents is not required to sell his animals right away. He may sell them a little at a time. In the same way, a גר who inherits dogs and pigs is not required to sell them right away. He may sell them a little at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא teaches a practical rule: someone who must get rid of forbidden animals may do it gradually.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forcing a sale of everything at once would mean a large money loss and could discourage people from doing תשובה. So the חכמים let them sell slowly. The rule for the גר shows the same kind of leniency for someone who suddenly owns animals he may not keep.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חכמים balanced strict rules against small animals with concern for people's livelihood and their path to תשובה.
steps.whatToRemember: A shepherd who does תשובה, or a גר who inherits forbidden animals, may get rid of them gradually instead of all at once.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A shepherd who repented,
phrases.notes: He is a shepherd of small animals, who until now grazed them on other people's land.

phrases.english: we do not require him to sell immediately,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מוֹכֵר עַל יָד עַל יָד.
phrases.english: rather he sells little by little.
And likewise, a convert who came to have
dogs and pigs in his inheritance,
we do not require him to sell immediately,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מוֹכֵר עַל יָד עַל יָד.
phrases.english: rather he sells little by little.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories about the sin of keeping animals to a practical rule about how a person stops keeping them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A repentant shepherd, and a גר who inherits dogs and pigs, may sell them gradually rather than all at once.

steps.title: A vow to buy a house or marry in Israel need not be fulfilled at once
steps.stepSummary: Someone who vowed to buy a house and marry a woman in ארץ ישראל is not forced to do it immediately. He may wait until he finds what suits him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, someone who vowed to buy a house and marry a woman in ארץ ישראל is not forced to do it right away. He may wait until he finds what is right for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the 'not all at once' idea from the last step. Now it applies that idea to a person who made a נדר to settle in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the shepherd and the גר may sell slowly, this person may take his time. The word וכן ('and similarly') ties it to the same principle. A person is not forced to rush into something that should be done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: to marry a woman (literally, 'to take a woman')
what is fitting or appropriate for him

phrases.english: And similarly, one who vowed
to buy a house and to marry a woman
in Eretz Yisrael
they do not obligate him to acquire immediately,
phrases.notes: He means he doesn't have to take the very first house or woman he finds.

phrases.english: until he finds what is appropriate for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'no rushing' principle from the shepherd and גר case to a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow to buy a house and marry in ארץ ישראל does not require acting immediately. One may wait for a fitting match.

steps.title: The woman who swore to marry anyone who came
steps.stepSummary: A woman upset by her son swore she would not turn away any man who came to marry her. Unworthy men rushed forward, and חכמים ruled that she only meant a fitting man.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman whose son was giving her trouble. In a rush she swore: 'Any man who comes, I will not turn him away.' Unworthy men jumped at the chance. When the case came before חכמים, they said: she only meant a man who is fitting for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story that backs up the last rule. A vow is understood as meaning only what is fitting and proper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words sounded like 'anyone at all.' חכמים said a person's oath is read by its sensible intention, not by its widest literal meaning. This supports the previous step, where the man only has to take what suits him.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: And there was an incident with a certain woman
whose son was causing her distress,
and she jumped up and swore:
"Anyone who comes, I will not turn him away,"
phrases.notes: She means any man who comes to marry her and deal with her son.

phrases.english: and people jumped at her
who were not worthy.
And when the matter came before the Sages,
they said: this woman did not intend
anyone except someone appropriate for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that supports reading a vow as meaning only what is fitting.
steps.raayaObject: That a vow to take something is understood as meaning only what is appropriate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the woman whose sweeping oath חכמים limited to a fitting man.
steps.whatToRemember: An oath or vow is read by its sensible intention. Saying 'anyone' is understood as 'anyone fitting.'

steps.title: No raising small wild animals, but רבי ישמעאל allows pest-catchers
steps.stepSummary: The ban on raising small domestic animals also covers small wild animals. רבי ישמעאל allows village dogs, cats, monkeys and חולדות סנאים because they clean the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as חכמים said one may not raise small domestic animals, they also said one may not raise small wild animals. רבי ישמעאל says: one may raise village dogs, cats, monkeys and genets, because they keep the house clean.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to the rule about raising animals. It extends the ban from sheep and goats to small wild animals as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part widens the ban to small wild animals too. רבי ישמעאל then makes an exception for animals that serve a useful purpose, getting rid of mice and pests in the house. Because they help, raising them is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind of small animal that catches pests (genets)
to clean out the house (of pests)

phrases.english: Just as they said
one may not raise small domestic animals,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָמְרוּ אֵין מְגַדְּלִין חַיָּה דַּקָּה.
phrases.english: so they said one may not raise small wild animals.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
one may raise village dogs,
and cats, and monkeys, and genets –
because they serve to clean the house.
phrases.notes: Clean the house of mice and other pests.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָמְרוּ אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the vow cases to the main topic of raising animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small wild animals may not be raised. רבי ישמעאל allows animals that rid the house of pests.

steps.title: What are חולדות סנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what animal the ברייתא means by חולדות סנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are חולדות סנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what an unfamiliar word in רבי ישמעאל's list means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other animals on the list are well known, but חולדות סנאים is not. The question is only about identifying the animal, not about the law.

phrases.english: What are genets?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term in רבי ישמעאל's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the animal called חולדות סנאים.

steps.title: רב יהודה identifies the animal
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says it is the שרצא חרצא. Others call it חרזא, an animal with short legs that grazes among thorn bushes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it is the שרצא חרצא. Some say it is called חרזא. Its legs are short, and it grazes among the thorn bushes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by giving the animal's everyday Aramaic name. A second version gives a slightly different name and describes the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions differ only on the name, חרצא or חרזא. The description helps the learner picture it: a short-legged creature living among thorns.

keyTerms.meaning: the Aramaic name for this animal

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: shartza chartza.
And some say: charza –
whose thighs are short,
and it grazes among the thorn bushes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what חולדות סנאים are.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the שרצא חרצא (or חרזא), a short-legged animal that grazes among thorns.

steps.title: Why the animal is called שרצא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it is called שרצא and answers that its legs are so short it seems to creep.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called שרצא? Because its legs are low.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the name contains the word for a creeping creature, and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרצא sounds like שרץ, something that slithers or creeps instead of walking. This animal does have legs, but they are so short that it looks like it creeps. That explains the name and closes the discussion of the term.

phrases.english: And why is it called shartza?
Because its thighs are low.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the name given in the previous answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an animal with legs is called by a name meaning 'creeping thing.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Its legs are so short that it looks like it creeps along the ground.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל allows raising animals that rid the house of pests. חולדות סנאים are short-legged creatures, which is why they are called שרצא.

steps.title: Babylonia took on the ban against raising small animals
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: in Babylonia we chose to act like ארץ ישראל and not raise בהמה דקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: In Babylonia we have made ourselves like ארץ ישראל regarding small animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement: the Jews of Babylonia chose to follow the ban on raising sheep and goats, even though the חכמים made that rule for ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on raising בהמה דקה was made for ארץ ישראל, because these animals graze in other people's fields and damage them. רב says that the Jews in Babylonia took the same ban on themselves. This sets up the question that comes next about רב הונא's own animals.

keyTerms.meaning: We made ourselves, meaning we chose to act like
Small domestic animals, such as sheep and goats

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
We have made ourselves, in Babylonia,
like Eretz Yisrael with regard to small animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: עָשִׂינוּ עַצְמֵנוּ בְּבָבֶל כְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the animals allowed in step 12 to step 15, the גמרא now teaches that the ban also took hold in Babylonia.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jews in Babylonia took on the ארץ ישראל ban against raising בהמה דקה.

steps.title: רב אדא asks רב הונא about his own animals
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks רב הונא how he can keep his own sheep and goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רב הונא: What about yours?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רב הונא: if Babylonia keeps the ban, why do you raise small animals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words look like a simple question, but they work as a challenge. רב הונא seems to be acting against the practice that רב just described.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rav Huna:
What about yours?
phrases.notes: He means: what about your own sheep and goats? Why are you raising them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרַב הוּנָא: דִּידָךְ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's statement to challenge רב הונא's behavior.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's practice of raising small animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If Babylonia took on the ban, רב הונא should not keep בהמה דקה.

steps.title: רב הונא says his wife חובה guards the animals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that his wife חובה watches the animals, so they do not damage anyone's field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Ours, חובה watches over them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself: his animals are carefully watched by his wife חובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban is that the animals graze in other people's fields. רב הונא claims that this worry does not apply to him, because his animals are guarded.

keyTerms.meaning: חובה, the name of רב הונא's wife

phrases.english: He said to him: Ours,
Hova watches over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּידַן קָא מְינַטְּרָא לְהוּ חוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the animals are guarded
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא is breaking the ban.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the animals are guarded, רב הונא thinks the reason for the ban does not apply.

steps.title: רב אדא curses רב הונא and the curse comes true
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא does not accept the answer and curses: may חובה bury her children. During רב אדא's lifetime, no children of רב הונא from חובה survived.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May חובה bury her son. All the years of רב אדא בר אהבה, no children survived for רב הונא from חובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא rejects רב הונא's answer in a sharp way, with a curse. The גמרא then tells us that the curse came true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא's anger shows that he did not accept guarding as a good enough reason to keep small animals. The story shows how seriously the ban was taken. The curse lasted only as long as רב אדא was alive.

keyTerms.meaning: All his years, meaning his whole life

phrases.english: He said to him: May Hova bury her son!
phrases.notes: This is a curse from רב אדא. He does not accept רב הונא's answer.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ שְׁנֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: All the years of Rav Adda bar Ahava,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אִקַּיַּים זַרְעָא לְרַב הוּנָא מֵחוּבָּה.
phrases.english: no children of Rav Huna from Hova survived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's answer from step 18 and gives the outcome of the story.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב הונא's claim that guarded animals are allowed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אדא held that guarding does not excuse keeping small animals once the ban was taken on.
steps.whatToRemember: Babylonia took on the ban against raising small animals, and רב אדא treated even רב הונא's guarded flock as a serious violation.

steps.title: Another version: the practice began when רב came to Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: Some say the statement came from רב הונא in the name of רב, and that it adds that this practice started when רב arrived in Babylonia.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב הונא said that רב said: We in Babylonia made ourselves like ארץ ישראל regarding small animals, from when רב came to Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב's statement. In this version it is quoted by רב הונא, and it adds when the practice started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things change in this version: the one quoting רב is רב הונא, not רב יהודה, and it adds a time, namely from when רב came to Babylonia. That suggests רב himself brought this practice to Babylonia.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule. It is the same statement as step 16, told in a different way, with a different person quoting it and an added time.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
We have made ourselves, in Babylonia,
like Eretz Yisrael with regard to small animals,
from when Rav came to Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of step 16's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Babylonian practice of keeping the ban began when רב arrived in Babylonia.

steps.title: רב, שמואל and רב אסי arrive at a celebration
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: רב, שמואל and רב אסי came to a celebration for a baby boy, and רב would not go in before שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, שמואל and רב אסי happened to come to a 'week of the son' celebration, and some say a 'redemption of the son' celebration. רב would not enter before שמואל,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new story. It sets the scene and tells us that רב would not walk in ahead of שמואל. The reason comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of what the event was. One version says it was a celebration a week after a boy's birth, at the ברית מילה. The other version says it was a פדיון הבן. The detail that רב would not enter before שמואל sets up what the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: The week of the son, a celebration around the ברית מילה
The redemption of the son, meaning פדיון הבן

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel and Rav Asi
happened to come to a house of 'the week of the son,'
phrases.notes: This was a celebration a week after a boy was born, at his ברית מילה.

phrases.english: and some say, to a house of 'the redemption of the son.'
Rav would not enter before Shmuel,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל וְרַב אַסִּי אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי שְׁבוּעַ הַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about רב, שמואל and רב אסי at a celebration.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: at the celebration, רב would not enter ahead of שמואל.
